title: Homes for sale rose 7.4% in October as contract signings fell 17%
dek: Realtor.com's October report shows more listings sitting on the market and fewer buyers signing contracts as mortgage rates held above 7%.

body.h: How many homes were for sale in October?

body.p: Active listings reached 1,183,500 homes nationally in October 2026, up 7.4% from a year earlier, according to Realtor.com's monthly housing report published November 4. Inventory is now about 6.6% below typical pre-pandemic levels, the narrowest gap since the pandemic.
Contract signings fell 17.0% from a year earlier, and the number of listings in pending status was down 10.5%. Realtor.com tied the slowdown to mortgage rates above 7%.

body.h: Are sellers listing fewer homes too?

body.p: Yes. New listings fell 7.5% from a year earlier to 357,000. Inventory still grew because homes already on the market stayed listed longer: the median home spent 63 days on the market, one day more than a year earlier.
The national median list price was $415,000, down 2.2% from a year earlier. About 20.5% of listings had a price cut.

body.h: Which regions saw the biggest changes?

body.p: Inventory grew fastest in the Northeast (up 16.5%) and Midwest (up 13.8%), with the West up 9.0% and the South up 3.8%. The South had the longest typical time on market at 69 days. For buyers in Texas and Oklahoma, that means more choice and more room to negotiate than a year ago, though higher rates still raise the monthly payment.

sources.label: Realtor.com Economic Research, October 2026 Monthly Housing Trends (Nov. 4, 2026)
